proposal: The Mandate recommends dividing OMB's six Resource Management Offices into smaller subject-matter areas, creating more political Program Associate Director posts, each paired with a Deputy PAD, to give the Director more direction over policy at agencies.
remaining: OMB would have to announce or staff additional PAD and Deputy PAD positions covering narrower subject areas.

status_summary: No public record was found of OMB splitting its six Resource Management Offices or creating additional PAD and Deputy PAD positions since 2025-01-20. OMB's apportionment delegation notices (effective 2025-02-11 and 2025-04-18) refer to the existing Program Associate Director and Deputy Associate Director structure without describing new offices.

timeline.event: OMB delegated apportionment authority to its Program Associate Directors; the notice names no new or split offices.
A second OMB delegation notice took effect, setting a succession order through Deputy Associate Directors, Branch Chiefs and other PADs of the existing structure; it names no new or split offices.

title: Divide OMB's six resource management offices into smaller areas with more political PADs
uncertainties: No public record was found of OMB splitting its six Resource Management Offices or creating additional Program Associate Director and Deputy posts since 2025-01-20. Federal Register searches returned only the 2025 apportionment delegation notices, which describe the existing structure; a congress.gov and govinfo search found no related bill, though enacted 119th Congress laws were not read for OMB staffing provisions; the whitehouse.gov OMB page shows no office structure; one news search found no reporting. The OMB list in the reginfo.gov Unified Agenda (Agency Rule List - 2026, 12 rules) holds no entry on the subject, and internal staffing would not normally appear there. An unannounced reorganization cannot be excluded. Checked systematically on 2026-10-19.
